frozen.selection_rule: Success, verification, defects, first review, review calls; baseline wins ties.
frozen.promotion: Evaluation only. No live lesson or deployment changes.

candidate-1.procedure:
Add an artifact-bound checkpoint to Oak’s existing render–inspect–repair loop. All supplied tasks ultimately passed structural checks and had no reported material visual defect; two runs contained a failed render, and one needed another review after technical properties remained unverified. This supports a conservative evidence-handling improvement, not a broad workflow replacement.

1. Before rendering, separate the brief into visual requirements and properties requiring file inspection. Preserve every requirement verbatim in the working checklist.
2. After each render, establish whether it succeeded and which artifact revision it produced. Never inspect a stale artifact as evidence for a failed or newer render. Keep the last successful revision available without modifying immutable sources.
3. Inspect the successful artifact visually and verify its required technical properties using the existing permitted checks. Associate views, extraction facts and check results with that same revision. Appearance alone does not establish encoding, exact color, opacity or audio absence.
4. If rendering fails, use the available diagnostic to make a bounded correction; do not infer a cause from failure alone. If inspection reveals a defect, name the violated requirement and make the smallest justified repair. Re-render and recheck the affected requirement plus potential regressions.
5. Supply the independent reviewer with the current artifact, source references and relevant artifact-bound facts. Preserve unknowns and limitations explicitly; do not reinterpret an unverified result as a visual defect or a pass. Any subsequent review must address changed evidence or an actual repair, not merely seek a different verdict.

Retain the existing model, permissions, immutable-source rules, independent reviewer, maximum of four review calls, and delivery policy. Deliver only under that policy, using the exact validated revision and accurately reporting unresolved limitations.
candidate-1.hypothesis: On comparable tasks, artifact-bound checkpoints will reduce reviews left unresolved solely because available technical facts were omitted, without increasing total tool calls or introducing material defects. Track failed renders, stale-evidence incidents, unresolved technical checks, tool calls and independently assessed defects. The hypothesis is unsupported if evidence-related uncertainty does not decrease or the added checkpoint increases work without improving evidence completeness. The supplied runs do not establish a recurring visual weakness or the causes of render failures.

candidate-2.procedure:
Add a source-envelope check before layout or motion repair. The supplied repairs already preserved complete artwork and corrected clipping, collisions and motion successfully; no recurring source-handling defect is demonstrated. Treat this as a small preventive check rather than a new design system.

1. Inspect each supplied source in its assigned role. Record its aspect ratio and complete visible extent, including thin extensions, tails and detached-looking details. For repairs, use the broken candidate to identify symptoms, not as authority for source geometry or intended wording. Keep all source files immutable.
2. For static media, reserve the brief’s required clear edge region and allocate distinct space for required text and artwork. Fit artwork proportionally, preserving its abstract appearance and any required completeness. Measure the rendered text extent rather than assuming the nominal text box contains every glyph. Check wording, clipping, collisions and separation against the source and brief before adding optional decoration.
3. For animation, keep the designated background stationary and move only the designated subject. Plan the path using the complete subject envelope rather than its center or most prominent shape. Check the envelope throughout the trajectory, including endpoints and rise/fall extrema; endpoint safety alone is insufficient. Preserve the supplied style and do not substitute whole-background movement, a slideshow or a repeated still.
4. Inspect the encoded result, not just the planned composition. For static work, compare the full view and relevant detail views with the sources. For motion, inspect beginning, ending, extrema and consecutive intermediate frames to verify direction, continuity, complete subject visibility and background stability. Distinct sampled frames establish change, not necessarily correct motion. If samples leave uncertainty, extend inspection rather than claiming complete coverage.
5. Repair only the demonstrated constraint violation, then repeat source comparison and regression checks on the new artifact. Preserve all technical validation and independent visual review.

Keep the task requirements, existing model, permissions, immutable sources, independent reviewer, four-review maximum and delivery policy unchanged. Do not use this check to relax validation or tune submissions merely to receive a pass.
candidate-2.hypothesis: A source-envelope check will catch clipping, distortion, text collisions or incorrect motion before independent review on comparable repair tasks, without increasing material defects or median production time. Record constraint violations found before review, defects found independently afterward, source fidelity and elapsed time. If it adds work but catches no additional violations and does not reduce downstream repairs, the proposed benefit is not supported. Existing evidence shows successful source-aware repairs, so any expected improvement is modest.

limitations: Twelve synthetic tasks; small directional pilot, not a population estimate.
One repetition by default; repeats are set before development.
Independent visual model review and structural checks are not human aesthetic judgments.
No production memories imported; no live Telegram delivery or external media provider.
Candidates receive a shared isolated local Python/Pillow/FFmpeg tool adapter.
Held-out feedback cannot be used to revise a procedure in this experiment.
